change: Map enabled semantics to both AT-SPI ENABLED and SENSITIVE; disabled controls have neither state.
old_result: Native provider regression failed because the enabled Designer TreeItem lacked SENSITIVE. Orca generated window grayed and button grayed requests for usable windows and Save.
fixed_result: Native provider regression passes ENABLED/SENSITIVE for root, TreeItem and editable field and clears both for the disabled field; normal Unicode editing, history, ThemeScope and save/reopen pass. Orca generated window. and button. requests and no grayed request in the retained run.

orca_diagnostic.session: GNOME Wayland with native Xwayland; isolated D-Bus session
orca_diagnostic.monitor: Temporary wrapper captures only calls to Orca debug.print_message for SPEECH OUTPUT and traces event types; it runs the installed Orca and does not synthesize speech. No installed reader source or user settings were changed.
orca_diagnostic.timing: The old driver waited 120 seconds after window focus and 60 seconds for each action; fixed driver used 120 seconds and 15 seconds. State getter failure/pass is independent of those timing differences.

limitations: Generated speech requests are diagnostic evidence, not a recording of audible output or an operator-signed reader record.
Field labels and roles are observed; full Unicode value/caret/selection/IME speech coverage is not proven.
The sample uses Xwayland inside GNOME Wayland, not an independent X11 desktop.
The monitor and driver are retained reproduction artifacts, not the normal acceptance workflow.
Windows Narrator/NVDA, macOS VoiceOver, real IME, Inspector, physical DPI, drag/drop, clean-machine packaging and complete record.json remain unproven.
